title: Portfolio (Home)
intro: The Portfolio tab: what needs attention, the totals, the charts, coverage per property, the debt-service forecast, rate shock, and every loan grouped by property.

topics.title: Needs Attention
topics.intro: The strip at the top: what is coming up in your loans, and which loans look worth refinancing.

steps.title: The cards
steps.text: Needs Attention lists, soonest first: balloons coming due in the next 24 months (Maturity), interest-only periods ending in the next 12 months (IO step-up), adjustable-rate resets in the next 12 months (ARM reset), and loans you flagged as out of date (Out of date). After those come the loans priced above today’s market (Refi). A card with a pink outline is three months away or less. Scroll the strip sideways to see every card. The picture is taken on a wide window so more cards show.

marks.label: Needs Attention
marks.text: The strip’s title; the red number is how many cards there are.

marks.label: ARM reset (amber)
marks.text: An adjustable rate resets soon: the new rate and the date.

marks.label: Maturity (red)
marks.text: A loan comes due: the balloon to pay off and the date.

marks.label: IO step-up (orange)
marks.text: An interest-only period ends: the new monthly payment and the date it starts.

steps.title: Refinance cards
steps.text: At the end of the strip are green Refi cards: loans whose rate is more than 0.25% above what the same loan would cost today. Each says by how much. Click one to open the refinance for that loan.

marks.label: Refi (green)
marks.text: Priced above today’s market — click to open its refinance.

marks.label: Another Refi card
marks.text: Sorted by how far above market, the biggest gap first.

steps.title: Click a date card
steps.text: Click a Maturity, IO step-up or ARM reset card: the app switches to Specific Property, opens that loan and brings its payment schedule to the month of the event, lit up for a few seconds. Scroll up and click Whole Portfolio to come back.

marks.label: That month
marks.text: The payment where the event happens (here the final payment with the balloon), lit up for a few seconds.

marks.label: Pays on
marks.text: The date the payment is due — the date on the card.

steps.title: Click a refinance card
steps.text: Click a Refi card and the refinance analysis opens for that loan: what it would cost today, and whether to refinance. The Refinance chapter explains that page. Close takes you back.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The refinance for the loan on the card (the Refinance chapter).

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to where you were.

topics.title: The totals
topics.intro: The four tiles under the heading: the whole book in four numbers.

steps.title: The four tiles
steps.text: The tiles are figures to read, not buttons. Every active loan counts; removed, paid-off and archived ones don’t. Portfolio DSCR = the total NOI of every property ÷ the total yearly principal-and-interest payments of every loan (during an interest-only period the full amortizing payment is used). Portfolio debt yield = total NOI ÷ total balance. A property with no NOI yet counts as $0 NOI — so its debt pulls both numbers down — and the tile says how many such properties there are. The targets (1.25×, 8% …) are set in Settings.

marks.label: 29 loans
marks.text: How many active loans the page covers.

marks.label: Priced above market
marks.text: How many properties pay more than 0.25% above today’s market rate (the Refi cards in Needs Attention).

marks.label: Total Debt Outstanding
marks.text: What is owed today on every loan; under it, the number of loans and what they were when first made.

marks.label: Weighted-Avg Rate
marks.text: The average interest rate, weighted by balance; under it, the total monthly debt service (payments plus escrows and fees).

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total yearly loan payments, against your minimum DSCR target.

marks.label: Portfolio Debt Yield
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total balance, against your minimum debt-yield target.

topics.title: The charts
topics.intro: Three charts: what kind of debt you have, when it comes due, and how the portfolio stands against its targets.

steps.title: Rate type, maturities and targets
steps.text: Point at a bar in “Debt maturing by year” to see its amount. In “Coverage vs targets” each bar is the portfolio’s figure and the thin dark line is your target: green clears it, amber is close, red is off. Under the bars, every property that is off a target is named — “no NOI” means its T12 or NOI hasn’t been added yet.

marks.label: Debt by rate type
marks.text: Today’s balance split into fixed, hybrid ARM and floating; the total in the middle.

marks.label: Legend
marks.text: Each type’s colour and its balance.

marks.label: A year’s maturities
marks.text: What comes due that year. Amber = in the next two years, green = later.

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Against your minimum DSCR.

marks.label: Portfolio LTV
marks.text: Balance ÷ value (value = NOI ÷ cap rate), against your maximum LTV — lower is better here.

marks.label: Portfolio Debt Yield
marks.text: Against your minimum debt yield.

marks.label: Off a target
marks.text: Every property that misses a target or has no NOI yet.

topics.title: Coverage per property
topics.intro: The table of every property against the three targets, with its rate against today’s market — and what to do next for each.

steps.title: The coverage table
steps.text: One row per property (a senior loan and its mezzanine count as one), worst DSCR first; properties with no NOI yet are at the bottom. The picture shows the first rows — the table lists every property. Current is the property’s rate today, Market is what the same loan would cost now, and Gap is the difference (green when it is more than 0.25% above market).

marks.label: Coverage
marks.text: DSCR, debt yield and LTV per property, against your targets.

marks.label: Create a portfolio…
marks.text: Put several properties under one new loan (last step of this topic).

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: The property’s yearly net operating income.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ yearly loan payments. Green clears the target, amber is close, red is off.

marks.label: Debt Yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ balance.

marks.label: LTV
marks.text: Balance ÷ value (value = NOI ÷ cap rate).

marks.label: Current
marks.text: The rate the property pays now (blended across its loans).

marks.label: Market
marks.text: What the same loan would cost today, from today’s rates.

marks.label: Gap
marks.text: Current minus Market. Green: worth looking at a refinance.

marks.label: Clears
marks.text: Meets all three targets.

marks.label: Off target
marks.text: Misses at least one target.

marks.label: Needs T12/NOI
marks.text: No NOI yet — add the T12 in Underwriting, or type the NOI (Add NOI).

marks.label: Refi path
marks.text: Opens the refinance for this property.

marks.label: Add NOI
marks.text: Type the property’s NOI (next step).

steps.title: Add NOI
steps.text: Click Add NOI on a property with no NOI. Type its yearly NOI, and the cap rate if you have a better one than the default for its type (value = NOI ÷ cap rate, which gives the LTV). Continue saves both; the row then shows its DSCR, debt yield and LTV, and every total on the page counts it. Cancel closes without saving. (The figure in the picture is made up and was not saved.)

marks.label: Annual NOI
marks.text: This window asks for one property’s NOI.

marks.label: Property annual NOI
marks.text: The yearly NOI in dollars, from the property’s operating statement. It must be more than $0.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Used to estimate the value (NOI ÷ cap rate) and so the LTV. Filled in by property type; change it if you have a better figure.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without saving.

marks.label: Continue
marks.text: Saves the NOI and cap rate; the table and the totals update.

steps.title: Refi path
steps.text: Click Refi path on a property that has an NOI: the refinance analysis opens for that property (all its loans together when it has more than one). The Refinance chapter explains that page. Close brings you back.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The refinance for that property.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio page.

steps.title: Create a portfolio…
steps.text: “Create a portfolio…” is for putting several properties under one new loan. It opens this list: tick every property the new loan will cover (type in the box to find one). Under the list the app adds up what is owed on them and their NOI, and names any property with no NOI yet. Create the portfolio opens the refinance of them together — nothing changes until you save the new loan there (the Refinance chapter). Cancel closes the list.

marks.label: Create a portfolio
marks.text: One new loan on several properties.

marks.label: Find a property
marks.text: Type part of a name to shorten the list.

marks.label: Tick
marks.text: Tick each property the new loan will cover.

marks.label: Owes / NOI
marks.text: What is owed on the property today, and its NOI (or “no NOI” when its T12 isn’t in yet).

marks.label: Totals
marks.text: How many are ticked, the loans that would be paid off and what they owe, and the NOI together.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the list.

marks.label: Create the portfolio
marks.text: Opens the refinance of the ticked properties (tick at least two).

topics.title: Forecast and rate shock
topics.intro: What the book will cost to carry in the years ahead, and what a rise in rates would do.

steps.title: Debt-Service Forecast
steps.text: Each bar is a year’s debt service (principal and interest plus escrows and fees), from this year on; this year’s bar is darker and its label bold. Point at a bar to see its amount. 1yr / 3yr / 5yr groups the years into one-, three- or five-year bars. Recurring shows only the regular payments; + Payoffs adds the balloons coming due on top of each bar.

marks.label: Debt-Service Forecast
marks.text: Yearly debt service ahead.

marks.label: 1yr
marks.text: One bar per year (shown).

marks.label: 3yr
marks.text: One bar per three years.

marks.label: 5yr
marks.text: One bar per five years.

marks.label: Recurring
marks.text: Regular payments only (shown).

marks.label: + Payoffs
marks.text: Adds the balloons due (next step).

marks.label: This year
marks.text: This year’s debt service.

steps.title: Three-year bars with payoffs
steps.text: Here 3yr and + Payoffs are on: each bar covers three years, and the dark part on top is the balloons that come due in those years. The key under the chart names the two colours.

marks.label: 3yr
marks.text: On: three-year bars.

marks.label: + Payoffs
marks.text: On: balloons stacked on top.

marks.label: A three-year bar
marks.text: Green: debt service. Dark: balloons due.

marks.label: Key
marks.text: Which colour is which.

steps.title: Rate Shock
steps.text: What happens to your payments if rates move. Fixed loans don’t move; floating loans move at once; hybrid ARMs move only when they reset. The table shows the blended rate, the monthly debt service and the extra (or saved) interest per year if rates fall 1%, stay, or rise 1% or 2%.

marks.label: Rate Shock
marks.text: How much of the book is floating or ARM, and what share that is.

marks.label: Fixed / ARM / Floating
marks.text: The book split by rate type: green fixed, amber ARM, red floating.

marks.label: Scenarios
marks.text: −100 bps, Today, +100 bps, +200 bps (100 bps = 1%): blended rate, monthly debt service, and interest per year more (red) or less (green) than today.

marks.label: In plain words
marks.text: What each +1% costs per year, and its share of your yearly debt service.

marks.label: Now or at reset
marks.text: How much moves at once (floating) and how much only when the ARMs reset.

marks.label: Most exposed
marks.text: The largest floating and ARM loans.

topics.title: Every loan, by property
topics.intro: Portfolio detail: one row per property, its loans under it, and a filter by lender.

steps.title: The Properties table
steps.text: Every property, largest balance first. A property with one loan is one row; click it to open that loan. A property with a senior loan and a mezzanine shows one bold row with the number of loans — click it to show them. Properties with no loan yet are at the bottom. The picture shows the first rows.

marks.label: Portfolio detail
marks.text: Every loan, grouped by property.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: The table.

marks.label: Top lender
marks.text: Which lender holds the most of your debt, and its share.

marks.label: All lenders
marks.text: Filter the table by lender (a later step).

marks.label: A property with 2 loans
marks.text: Click to show (or hide) its loans. Its row shows the combined balance, blended rate and total monthly P&I.

marks.label: A one-loan property
marks.text: Click to open its loan.

marks.label: Status
marks.text: The loan’s status (Active, or a flag such as Out of date).

steps.title: Show a property’s loans
steps.text: Clicking the bold row opens it: each loan is listed under it, marked Senior or Mezz, with its own lender, type, balance, rate, payment and maturity. Click the bold row again to close it. Click a loan to open it.

marks.label: Open property
marks.text: Click again to close it.

marks.label: Senior loan
marks.text: The first-lien loan. Click to open it.

marks.label: Mezz loan
marks.text: The mezzanine loan behind it. Click to open it.

steps.title: Open a loan
steps.text: Clicking a loan opens it on the Specific Property side: its figures, its payment schedule and the property’s profile (the property chapters explain that page). Click Whole Portfolio to come back.

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: Now showing one property.

marks.label: The loan
marks.text: The loan you clicked; pick another here.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio page.

steps.title: Filter by lender
steps.text: Click All lenders: every lender is listed with its total balance. Tick one or more and the table keeps only their properties (a property with two loans opens to show the matching one). The button and the line beside it say how many lenders are picked and their share of the book. Clear takes the filter off.

marks.label: Filter by lender
marks.text: Every lender in the book.

marks.label: Ticked
marks.text: Only this lender’s loans are shown.

marks.label: Balance
marks.text: What is owed to that lender.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Shows every lender again.

marks.label: 1 lender
marks.text: How many lenders are picked.

marks.label: Share
marks.text: Their share of the whole book.

topics.title: Add a property
topics.intro: Add a property from the Portfolio page — a name is enough to start.

steps.title: Add Property
steps.text: Click Specific Property, then Add Property. Type the property’s name and click Create. That is all it needs: its loans, T12, rent roll and documents can come later. The property is added to the portfolio straight away.

marks.label: Add a property
marks.text: Adds a property to the portfolio.

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: The name only (a made-up one here).

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without adding anything.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Adds the property.

steps.title: It joins the portfolio
steps.text: The new property is at the bottom of the Properties table, marked No loan yet. Click it to open it in Underwriting, where its T12 goes and its loan can be added. It also counts in the property count at the top, and in coverage, where its NOI will count once it has one.

marks.label: The new property
marks.text: Click to open it in Underwriting.

marks.label: No loan yet
marks.text: It has no loan yet.

steps.title: A name it can’t take as is
steps.text: If the name is empty, the window asks for one. If the name is like a property you already have, the app asks first: Open it opens the one you have; Create anyway adds the new one; Cancel does nothing. (The exact name of a property you have isn’t added twice — the app says so. The name of one of your loans offers to add a loan to that property instead.)

marks.label: Similar to …
marks.text: The property it looks like.

marks.label: Which one
marks.text: The name you typed and the one you already have.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is added.

marks.label: Create anyway
marks.text: Adds the new property — they are different buildings.

marks.label: Open it
marks.text: Opens the property you already have.

topics.title: Removed, paid-off and archived
topics.intro: At the bottom of the page: loans and properties taken out of the totals, and how to bring them back.

steps.title: Removed loans and archived properties
steps.text: A loan you remove (on its Loan Record) or mark as paid off leaves every total, tile and the calendar, and is listed in the grey strip with its status and the date. Restore puts it back exactly as it was. A property you archive (Specific Property → Remove) leaves the lists, the totals and the count with all its loans, and is listed in the amber strip; its files stay. Click its name to bring it back. Each bin deletes for good — it asks first (next steps).

marks.label: Removed & paid-off loans
marks.text: How many loans are out of the totals.

marks.label: The loan
marks.text: Its name, its status (Removed or Paid off) and the date.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Puts it back in every total, tile and the calendar.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes the loan record (asks first).

marks.label: Archived
marks.text: How many properties are archived.

marks.label: Un-archive
marks.text: Click the name: the property and its loans come back to the lists, the totals and the count.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes the property and its files (asks first).

steps.title: Delete a loan permanently
steps.text: The bin asks first. Delete permanently removes the loan record for good — the app can’t undo it, but the automatic backups (Data menu) keep a copy. The property stays, with its files. Cancel leaves everything as it is.

marks.label: Delete permanently?
marks.text: The loan it is about.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: Gone for good; the automatic backups keep a copy.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the loan in the list.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes the record.

steps.title: Delete an archived property
steps.text: The bin on an archived property lists what will be deleted — its loans and its files. It can’t be undone in the app; the automatic backups keep a copy, and portfolio chats that mention it are kept. Cancel leaves it archived.

marks.label: Delete permanently?
marks.text: The property it is about.

marks.label: What is deleted
marks.text: Everything that goes with it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps it archived.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes it for good.
